Based on the provided background, a good story provides the reader with a deeper understanding of human nature and unique viewpoints that challenge beliefs. Instead of taking the cliché route of reveling in the downfall of a "flawless" person or uncovering a dark secret, the narrator realizes that Quentin's curated perfection is just a better-executed version of his own nervous habits, offering the reader a compassionate and thought-provoking perspective on human defenses.
